title: The harness release candidate: every verify layer, the levels and the gate, broken alone
note: Killed without a signature runtime: each layer beneath SHA256SUMS has a forgery consistent everywhere else (tests/test_supply_chain.py), so a deleted check cannot hide behind the one above it, and the signature step is exercised through the Sigstore command it builds and an injected checker that the CLI cannot reach (tests/test_offline_verify.py, tests/test_release_admission.py). The real signature path runs in the supply-chain workflow, with GitHub OIDC, offline in a network namespace. SC1-SC20 were anchored in tools/supply_chain.py until D-2026-144 moved the verifier into tools/offline_verify.py; their names and rationales are unchanged. SC21-SC34 attack the non-interchangeable levels and the release gate (D-2026-143); SC35-SC48 the portable verifier's own inputs (D-2026-144).

mutations.name: SC14_members_the_manifest_does_not_list_are_accepted

mutations.name: SC19_verify_never_reads_the_archived_manifest

mutations.name: SC20_an_empty_manifest_describes_any_archive

mutations.name: SC21_a_digest_run_claims_a_signature

mutations.name: SC22_the_gate_takes_a_digest_run
